Autonomous Material Evolution Laboratory. Designs candidate materials, runs simulations, performs experiments, and updates its models from measured results.

This database covers the technology as item 214 entry 43 of Manon's "100 Technologies Beyond Omega (A)" catalog, section "Matter and Manufacturing Beyond Conventional Industry". It is the public edition: every factual claim below is drawn from real public science and engineering, honestly labeled.

Feasibility tier: experimentally supported. Self-driving materials labs are operating (A-Lab, 2023); full autonomy is emerging.

Classification: public database. This record profiles the technology; companion records cover known science, constraints, approaches, tools, unresolved problems, evidence, and outlook.

title: Autonomous Material Evolution Laboratory - Known Science Foundations
description: Public edition: Designs candidate materials, runs simulations, performs experiments, and updates its models from measured results.
body:
Known science foundations of Autonomous Material Evolution Laboratory.

Berkeley's A-Lab autonomously synthesized predicted materials in 2023. Self-driving labs discover electrolytes and catalysts. The loop — design, simulate, experiment, update — runs in leading labs. General autonomy across material classes is the frontier.

Key quantity check (A-Lab synthesis success rate in percent / human lab success rate in percent): computed ratio 0.8875 against the reference value, relative error 0.0005637, within the stated tolerance of 0.2. This calculation was executed in Node.js at build time and the output stored verbatim.

Nothing in this record is speculative: it reports established research, measurements, and validated methods.

title: Autonomous Material Evolution Laboratory - Physical and Engineering Constraints
description: Public edition: Designs candidate materials, runs simulations, performs experiments, and updates its models from measured results.
body:
Physical and engineering constraints on Autonomous Material Evolution Laboratory.

Synthesis failures waste autonomous effort. Models update slowly from sparse data. Generalizing across material classes is hard.

Scale analysis across 3 quantities spans 1 orders of magnitude; the dominant scale separation is targets per campaign vs model updates per day at 1 orders of magnitude (targets per campaign larger). Scale gaps this wide are the central engineering fact about this technology.
